    #73578. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1285 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1285 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The major prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.
    • There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.
    • Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The major prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

    Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

    Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

    Sources indicate that since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

    The recent track record here states this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

    Recent findings suggest that there isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

    Industry observers note that he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

    Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

    There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

    It has been revealed that we'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a latest procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

    The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

    According to recent reports, skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

    I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

    In a recent development, again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

    According to recent reports, for those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

    A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

    Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

    Gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

    It has been revealed that stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

    Justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

    Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

    According to recent reports, david Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

    Sources indicate that corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

    Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

    CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

    According to recent reports, max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

    We can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

    Industry observers note that by this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

    Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?".

    I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas.
    • Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.
    • We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that thursday marks the final day of the General Manager meetings in Las Vegas. Though we haven't seen any major moves this offseason, we have seen an uptick in rumors in the past few days and that isn't a coincidence. Put a bunch of reporters and front-office execs in the same area for three or four days and chatter picks up, even if there isn't a ton of actual substance behind it.

    Rumors are always fun, so let's round up the latest right here in addition to any news.

    We have one of our first major-league deals of the offseason as the Braves have signed reliever Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35 million deal. Phillips ranked No. 34 on our top 50 free agent list.

    Industry observers note that phillips, a 32-year-old right-hander, has been a setup man or closer for the Dodgers for the last several seasons. In returning from surgery last season, he appeared in 31 games, pitching to a 3.46 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 33 strikeouts in 26 innings. The majority of his closing experience came in 2023 when he had 24 saves in 27 chances.

    The Braves' closer last season was Raisel Iglesias, but he's a free agent. Holdover Robert Suarez could take over those duties while Phillips, lefty Dylan Lee and youngster Didier Fuentes are also in the late-inning mix.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blue Jays went from one of the best offensive teams in 2025 to one of the worst in 2026. They'd love a big bounceback from Vladimir Guerrero Jr., among other positive movements, but they also look for outside help. Might that help come in the form of free agent infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.?

    The Jays have met with representatives for Chisholm, reports Sportsnet.

    Chisholm, 28, hit .231/.312/.399 last season, but had a huge 2025 and any signing team would be hoping for the 2025 version of Chisholm.

    The Jays do have a capable incumbent second baseman in Ernie Clement, but either Clement or Chisholm can be used in the outfield and the Blue Jays certainly need outfield upgrades.

    The Phillies have been telling opposing teams that they are not "locked into anything" regarding their current outfield situation, according to The Athletic, so much so that All-Star outfielder Brandon Marsh is available in a trade.

    As things stand, with Bryce Harper moving back to first base, the Phillies would have Bryan De La Cruz in right, Justin Crawford in center and Marsh in left, but that all seems pretty fluid as they look to upgrade the ballclub and keep that window of contention open.

    Marsh, 28, had a stellar start last season, leading to his first-ever All-Star Game. Through July 1, he hit .319/.352/.530. The rest of the way, however, he slashed .177/.241/.241, dragging him down overall to a 90 OPS+ and 0.4 WAR on the season.

    The Mariners have shown interest in free agent left fielder Ian Happ, per MLB Network.

    Happ, 32, has spent his entire 10-year MLB career with the Cubs, who drafted him in the first round all the way back in 2015. He was pretty consistent from 2022-25, averaging 3.9 WAR with a .251/.347/.433 (118 OPS+) line and winning four Gold Gloves. Last season, though, he dipped to .218/.326/.412 (103 OPS+) with 2.7 WAR. He still topped 20 home runs for the fifth time in the last six years.

    The Mariners have a vacancy in left field with Randy Arozarena having hit free agency and a need to upgrade their offense.

    Yesterday's big news was the Yankees' interest in free agent first/third baseman Alec Bohm and The Athletic reports that we can now add the Mets to the list of suitors.

    Bohm hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with 15 home runs, 88 RBI and -0.2 WAR last season. It might be surprising to see him garnering such interest on the open market, but there isn't much right-handed power out there and Bohm finished last season strong (.318/.402/.453 in his last 42 games). The Mets, meanwhile, are desperate for help at the cold corner after last year's disastrous Jorge Polanco experiment. Jared Young did provide a glimmer of hope at first base before suffering a concussion in September while colliding with a teammate on a play.

    Free agent starting pitcher Dustin May has a decent market right now, according to MLB Network, with at least the Cubs, White Sox, Padres and Astros having shown interest in the right-hander.

    May, 29, made 31 starts between the Cardinals and Brewers last season, going 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 145 ⅔ innings. He revealed flashes of brilliance with the Cardinals and had a stretch from April 10 to June 15 during which he posted a 2.54 ERA in 12 starts, but in the end there was plenty of inconsistency and even bad, forcing him into a bullpen role in the playoffs for the champion Brewers.

    Free agent catcher Ryan Jeffers has been extended the qualifying offer from the Twins, meaning he has to decide by net Tuesday whether to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract or hit free agency. There's nothing that claims a team can't re-sign a player after he declines their qualifying offer, of course, and it sounds like that path is possible in this case.

    Jeffers will decline the QO and the Twins are interested in reaching a multi-year deal to bring him back, reports the Minnesota Star-Tribune. Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 with 14 home runs for Minnesota in 2026, a standout line for a catcher, though he missed several months with a broken hamate. The Twins do have several catchers in their farm system, including Vahn Lackey, the No. 3 pick in last year's draft, and Eduardo Tait, who headlined the trade return for Jhoan Duran.

    Much has been said and will continue to be said about the 2027 free agent class and how it looks relatively weak, especially on the position-player side, where the best players are the likes of Jazz Chisholm Jr., Seiya Suzuki, and the aforementioned Arozarena and Jeffers.

    As we know, the Rays love to find avenues where they can exploit market inefficiencies. Their latest move might be to hit the trade market with center fielder Jonny DeLuca in anticipation of moving Victor Mesa Jr. to center, according to The Athletic.

    According to recent reports, deLuca, 28, got more playing time than ever before in 2026, appearing in 112 games and getting 370 plate appearances. He hit .266/.300/.429 (101 OPS+) with 11 homers, 50 RBI, 17 steals and 1.7 WAR.

    In a recent development, fresh off a playoff berth despite the lowest payroll in all of baseball at a paltry $75ish million, the Guardians are planning to increase payroll. Or so they say.

    "We'll go up," club president Chris Antonetti told The Athletic. "We have to.".

    The Guardians hosted six playoff games and made some money there, not to mention that they have a bunch of players hitting arbitration and surely they want to spend more to remain competitive. There's an added wrinkle here, too, which would be that the ownership side is really pushing hard for a salary cap when the upcoming CBA expires in a few weeks. With a cap comes a floor and we've seen MLB float proposals with salary floors in the $180 million range, or well more than double what the Guardians had last season.

    So, yeah, I'd say the Guardians "have to" increase payroll, one way or another.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Published: 08:02 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 10:36 EST, 16 November 2026.

    Jurgen Klopp has called on FIFA's embattled president Gianni Infantino to resign, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

    Infantino's reputation took a nosedive after his sycophantic behaviour towards Donald Trump before and during the World Cup - most memorably by awarding him a 'FIFA Peace Prize'.

    And it only got worse when his clandestine plot to sell off stakes in the World Cup, a devious scheme which would have banked him millions, was revealed by The Times.

    Now Germany manager Klopp has hit out: 'There is now a unanimous consensus that a change would make sense.

    'I thought that, after Sepp Blatter, the situation couldn't get any worse - but here we are.

    'Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

    Jurgen Klopp has publicly savaged FIFA president Gianni Infantino, becoming the first national team manager to do so.

    The Germany manager noted Infantino - who tried to sell off stakes in the World Cup to his own benefit - is 'worse' than his predecessor Sepp Blatter.

    'Without a doubt, there are people who truly care about football and have no financial interests,' the former Liverpool manager noted.

    Infantino has clung on to his job thus far, surviving a crisis summit in Morocco in August, despite intense and widespread opposition.

    A total of 90 nations including all of UEFA's teams rebelled, with threats to boycott FIFA competitions, and Infantino's £3.1billion plan fell apart.

    But he still maintained a large swell of support among Africa, Asia, and South America - especially after offering each nation £30million if they supported his plan. His opponents pointed out that he could simply have given money from FIFA's cash reserves of roughly £4.5b.

    In the pages of this historic newspaper, football legend Luis Figo wrote that 'Infantino must go' and accused him of 'debasing the office of FIFA President'.

    FIFA does not have a history of picking good leaders - Blatter resigned in 2015 amid allegations of corruption, though he was cleared alongside Michel Platini last year.

    Infantino now looks well-placed to be re-elected for a fourth term in next March's presidential elections.

    The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

    Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, has agreed to run against Infantino and has the backing of UEFA's executive committee.

    '(Diallo has) extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023,' UEFA said.

    Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has already announced his intention to be a rival to Infantino.

    Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association, is also reportedly set to mount a challenge.

    Ex-Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was touted as a potential challenger but it is understood he told European football’s governing body UEFA that he would not stand.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA announced Thursday night.

    It has been revealed that the Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    Alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games. This time around, he avoided the IL and appeared in 158 games. He hit .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+) with 34 doubles, a triple, 42 home runs, 106 RBI, 105 runs and 6.8 WAR. He made a late run at the Triple Crown, missing out by one home run and seven RBI. He did lead the majors in all three triple slash categories, though, leading in average by five points, on-base percentage by a whopping 42 points -- he led the majors in walks -- and 31 points in slugging percentage. Add the latter two and his OPS victory was 90 points -- 1.033 to second place's .943 (National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong).

    The only players in MLB history to lead the majors in all three triple slash categories:.

    Alvarez becomes just the third Astros player to win MVP after Jeff Bagwell in 1994 and Jose Altuve in 2017.

    Rays third baseman Junior Caminero finished in second. At age 22, he played all 162 games, leading the Rays to the best AL record. He hit .276/.360/.524 (144 OPS+) with 42 home runs, 101 RBI and 100 runs, posting a 5.7 WAR. He's already made history, too, as the Rays had previously never had a player finish in the top five of MVP voting.

    It has been revealed that royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. came in third. This is now his fourth straight season in the top seven and third straight season in the top four. He finished second in 2024. This season, he hit .281/.359/.441 (125 OPS+) with 33 doubles, 18 homers, 54 RBI, 94 runs, 45 steals and 6.7 WAR.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team unveiled on Saturday.
    • Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position.
    • Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team unveiled on Saturday.

    Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

    Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

    Industry observers note that the 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

    According to recent reports, shesterkin was a massive reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

    Industry observers note that dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

    New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

    First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

    New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

    The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

    Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

    According to recent reports, however, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

    Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether Upcoming York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so rapidly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award for the 2026 season unanimously, the BBWAA revealed Thursday evening.

    It has been revealed that the Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing NL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

    According to recent reports, though the results were unsurprising by the time the year wound down, going back to the start of the season, this marks a huge upset. Shohei Ohtani was the overwhelming favorite to win the award heading into the season and maintained favorite status through the All-Star break. A combination of his injuries and PCA's monster season turned the tide late.

    Appearing in all 162 games, Crow-Armstrong hit .280/.372/.570 (156 OPS+) with 31 doubles, eight triples, 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs, 41 steals and 9.8 WAR. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and total bases while leading the NL in slugging, OPS and OPS+. He became the seventh player in MLB history to join the 40-40 club (40 home runs and 40 steals in the same season). Further, he led the majors in multiple advanced defensive metrics, putting together one of the great all-around seasons from a position player in recent memory.

    PCA joins the following list of Cubs to win MVP:.

    Sources indicate that ohtani, the four-time MVP, finishes in second. At the plate, Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512 with 26 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 81 RBI, 89 runs, 11 steals and 3.2 WAR. On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.

    It has been revealed that the nationally underrated Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finishes in third. He still hasn't made an All-Star Game, though he did start 2026 as a member of Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. In the regular season, Turang hit .268/.366/.450 (124 OPS+) with 37 doubles, three triples, 21 home runs, 100 RBI, 102 runs and 7.3 WAR, rating out as one of the best defenders in baseball.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.
    • Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors.
    • To answer that, we'll look backwards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs.

    Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors. He hit .280/.372/.570 with stellar defense, led the league in home runs (tied with Kyle Schwarber) and massively upgraded his on-base skills. Now, just a few months shy of his 25th birthday, he has an MVP to his name.

    So what's next? To answer that, we'll look backwards.

    Since integration, only eight center fielders have posted at least 8.0 WAR in a season age-25 or younger: Willie Mays, Mickey Mantle, Willie Davis, César Cedeño, Ken Griffey Jr., Andruw Jones, Mike Trout and PCA. The only ones to top PCA's 9.8 were Mays, Mantle and Trout. If we went back to pre-integration, Tris Speaker and Ty Cobb were the only others who bested PCA here.

    What road map will PCA's career follow?

    In a recent development, willie Davis was an inconsistent hitter through his age-23 season but had flashed a nice power-speed combo. Sound familiar? That gaudy 8.4 WAR total in 1964, though, was driven largely by monster defensive metrics. Davis hit .294/.316/.413 (110 OPS+) with 23 doubles, seven triples, 12 home runs, 77 RBI, 91 runs and 42 steals. There's little doubt that PCA's 2026 season dwarfed this one overall, and Davis was far behind Mays (11.0) for the league lead in WAR.

    For the rest of his career, Davis averaged 3.1 WAR per season, and though he had good years, he never reached 6.0 WAR again. The WAR figure was, again, mostly driven by defense. He had several good offensive seasons, but his only 20-homer season came in 1962 when he was 22, two years prior to his career year.

    Davis' career probably looks a lot like PCA's apparent upside before his home run barrage in the first half of 2025. He racked up over 60 career WAR with a decent batting average, excellent defense and excellent baserunning.

    With PCA reaching 30-30 last year and 40-40 this year, though, the bar has been raised.

    It has been revealed that césar Cedeño followed up his 8.0 WAR season with a 7.4 season at age 22 and 5.8 at age 23. He was very good through age 29 and, in fact, the most statistically similar player through both ages 27 and 28 was Hall of Famer Carl Yastrzemski. Things fell apart after that. As a quick and easy way to illustrate it, Cedeño amassed 49.4 WAR through his age-29 season and only 3.6 in his final six years.

    According to recent reports, it's easier to remember that Andruw Jones' career unfolded in similar fashion because we witnessed it not too long ago and then discussed his Hall of Fame candidacy during his nine turns on the ballot before he finally made it in. In Jones' 12 Braves' season, he racked up 368 home runs, 1,117 RBI and 61 WAR while generally being considered the best defensive center fielder in baseball. Once he left, in time for his age-31 season, Jones accrued just 1.7 WAR in his last five seasons.

    Through Jones' age-28 season, the most statistically similar players are Bryce Harper and Frank Robinson.

    To compare these two to Crow-Armstrong, the argument would be that he'll continue to look like one of the best players in baseball -- even if taking steps backward from being the very best in the 2026 regular season -- before falling apart once he's around 30 years old.

    According to recent reports, certainly possible, but given the adjustments he's already not only been willing to make at the plate, but eager to make, I'm just not seeing him all of a sudden hitting a wall. Sure, at some point he'll start losing speed and that'll affect his defensive range and baserunning, but why would the plate skills deteriorate all of a sudden?

    Then again, few saw it coming with Jones.

    All three of these players were on the path to having an argument as the best player in history before injuries derailed them in their 30s and left them as mere "all-time greats.".

    It has been revealed that through Mickey Mantle's age-30 season, he had 90.7 WAR. He averaged 121 games per year in his final six seasons, putting up 19.5 WAR. Through  Ken Griffey Jr.'s age-30 season, he had 76.2 WAR. He played 10 more seasons, but only amassed 7.6 more WAR. Through Mike Trout's age-27 season, he had 72.1 WAR (his top statistical similars were Mantle, Robinson and Griffey). We'll skip 2020 for obvious reasons, but since then he's averaged 90 games and 3.0 WAR per season.

    In a recent development, even with the drop-offs, it would be surprising to see Crow-Armstrong reach this level because it's surprising to see any player reach this lofty standard. In career WAR among center fielders, Mantle is fourth, Trout is fifth and Griffey is sixth. They trail only Cobb, Speaker and the guy we're going to discuss next. Joe DiMaggio is seventh.

    Despite the lofty standard PCA set for himself in 2026, coming close to Willie Mays' career would be jaw-droppingly shocking, and that is absolutely not intended as a slight.

    Recent findings suggest that mays has an argument as the greatest player in baseball history and he put himself in that discussion by being good at everything and doing it all with great longevity. From his age-23 to -35 seasons, he led the majors in WAR eight times, leading the NL an additional two times. His worst seasons in that timeframe were 7.6 and 7.8 WAR. In that span, he also led the league in runs twice, hits once, triples three times, home runs three times, stolen bases four times, average once, on-base percentage once, slugging percentage five times and OPS five times.

    Mays even posted 5.2 WAR at age 39 and 6.3 at age 40. He led the NL with a .425 OBP when he was 40 years old! He hit .345/.411/.667 at age 23.

    Mays' 156.2 career WAR ranks third among position players all-time behind two guys you might have heard of: Barry Bonds (162.8) and Babe Ruth (162.3).

    I feel pretty strongly Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't headed for a run at this career and that's just fine.

    The realistic long-term range for the 2026 National League MVP seems somewhere between Cedeño and Mantle. It's a wide variance of outcomes between those two, obviously, as well it should be when the player we discuss is only 24 years old. For his name to be mentioned among these at all is a testament to the year Crow-Armstrong just put together.

    #73553. Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (909 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m.
    • Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly.
    • Recent findings suggest that something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are almost certain to lock out the players at that time. Skubal is expected to sign before then.

    Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly. There's a real chance Skubal signs a contract worth more than $400 million in the next two weeks or so. Excluding Shohei Ohtani, who is technically a pitcher but is really a two-way player, here are the largest pitching contracts in history:.

    According to recent reports, 1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    Industry observers note that 2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Recent findings suggest that something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value. Several big-market clubs are said to be pursuing Skubal (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), who is a special free agent as an in-his-prime ace. Conditions are ripe for a record deal.

    Recent findings suggest that there is also a chance Skubal goes the Valdez route, or the Bo Bichette/Kyle Tucker route, and signs a short-term contract with a high annual salary. It might only be a small chance, but there is a chance. The Athletic reports the Dodgers prefer such an arrangement with Skubal. ESPN indicates Skubal has no interest in such a deal, though minds can always be changed.

    According to recent reports, with that in mind, here are the pros and cons of a high-dollar, short-term contract for Skubal. Keep in mind that such a contract is usually a three- or four-year deal with opt outs, not a straight one- or two-year contract, and Skubal wouldn't necessarily have to use the opt outs to re-enter free agency. He could leverage them into a new contract to stay with his team.

    It has been revealed that 1. Maximize earnings. Plain and simple, a short-term contract would give Skubal a chance to max out his earnings by making free agency available to him again as soon as next offseason. Go out, have a typical Skubal season in 2027, and perhaps market forces push the demand even higher than it is right now. Remember that, along with a salary cap, there could be a salary floor in the future. Small-market contenders like, say, the Guardians or Rays could throw many millions at Skubal to reach the floor in the future.

    According to recent reports, 2. Chance to set more records. This ties back to the last point. Skubal already set a upcoming salary record for an arbitration-eligible player ($32 million in 2026) and he's positioned to set a new standard for pitcher contracts this offseason. Go back into free agency in a year or two, and Skubal (and Boras) could have a chance to break his own pitcher contract record. The record itself won't be a driving factor in that decision (the money will ultimately decide things), but it would be a nice feather in his cap.

    3. Freedom to change teams. Sometimes things don't work out. I don't think Juan Soto expected to miss the postseason in the first two years of his record 15-year, $765 million contract with the Mets. It's entirely possible Skubal could find his next situation not to his liking for whatever reason. Maybe the team doesn't contend, maybe he clashes with the coaching staff, maybe he doesn't like the local breakfast taco options. There could be a million different reasons it doesn't work. A short-term, high-dollar deal would give Skubal an escape hatch and allow him to head elsewhere if things go sideways.

    1. Injury and performance risk. All things considered, Skubal is a pretty safe bet on a long-term contract, though he is a pitcher, and pitchers get hurt. It's what they do. Skubal has had three elbow surgeries, including Tommy John surgery in 2017 and a minor procedure this May. If he gets hurt again, or his performance slips for whatever reason, then he could wind up costing himself in the significant picture because he won't be able to opt out and sign a larger deal. A short-term, high-dollar contract will pay him handsomely. He won't struggle to put bread on the table. But injury/performance risk means Skubal could ultimately leave money on the table.

    Recent findings suggest that 2. Potential salary cap. It is possible the next CBA will include a salary cap, which could limit Skubal's market and earning potential should he go back out into free agency in a year or two (or three). It's not just the cap itself either. MLB has proposed contract limits as part of the salary cap: five years at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, or six years at 16% of the cap for players who remain with their current team. Even if MLB doesn't get a salary cap and instead the competitive balance tax system remains in place with stiffer penalties, that could cost Skubal in the future. This offseason might be his last chance to sign in a truly free market.

    One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

    In a recent development, that made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

    Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

    Recent findings suggest that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an concern is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    The Warriors went into survival mode the minute it was confirmed that Stephen Curry would miss at least the next two weeks, and perhaps more, with an oblique tear. And in their first test, Curry's absence was felt in a major way as the Spurs put a 38-point beating on them on Friday night.

    This was never going to end well. The Warriors would have been heavy underdogs in this game even had Curry played. But the Warriors were hoping to at least stay in the fight for a little while. Instead, they were the Michael Spinks to San Antonio's Mike Tyson as the Spurs scored the first 18 points of the game and never looked back.

    There are a few core things that need to happen for the Warriors to stay competitive while Curry is out, and it starts with Yaxel Lendeborg assuming full-time alpha status and producing like an All-Star with the defense now primarily focused on him.

    According to recent reports, it's a lot to ask of a rookie, but he's set the bar so high to start his career that he's proven capable. He's putting up north of 20 points per game on super efficient shooting through his first 12 games.

    Could he possibly do it again against the Spurs? The answer was an emphatic no. Lendeborg had three points on 1-of-13 shooting, and afterward he was beating himself up worse than the Spurs did.

    "We just got the s--t beat out of us," Lendeborg remarked. "I was flustered the entire game. I couldn't make a damn layup. I don't even know, man. ... I'm not going to move past this. Everybody is saying throw it out the window. I can't throw a damn thing out the window. We just lost by like a hundred. I'm f--ked up mentally right now.

    "It was an awful performance by me," Lendeborg continued. "I let everybody on this team down. I'm not gonna forget this ever. I don't remember the last time I got beat [like this] the whole entire game, with no hope at all. It felt helpless out there.".

    Recent findings suggest that helpless. It's a strong word, but appropriate on this night. Welcome to life without the greatest shooter and one of the greatest scorers to ever live commanding all the defensive attention and still putting up 30 a night.

    In a recent development, lendeborg's unfiltered commentary is refreshingly raw. He says exactly what is on his mind, and certainly you'd rather have a player be hard on himself after a performance like this than a guy who doesn't care. But it was, in the end, one game against probably the best team with the best player in the world.

    Lendeborg will be fine. If you're thinking he got exposed in this game, save it. This dude is for real. He'll discard this and get right for New Orleans on Monday, because at 8-5 the Warriors are still in good shape. They can't let this spiral and suddenly the next few weeks are undoing all the good work they did to start the season.

    In a recent development, steve Kerr started small against Victor Wembanyama, inserting De'Anthony Melton and Will Richard into the first five with Draymond Green at center. Bold move. The only way that can work is to run and gun, and Brandin Podziemski needed to be at the forefront of that attack. He wasn't.

    In a recent development, podziemski, who has been terrific to start the season, averaging nearly 17 points per game and hitting 2.8 3-pointers a night at a 40% clip, finished with eight points on 2-of-10 shooting in San Antonio. Do the math, and Podziemski and Lendeborg, the Warriors' top two offensive options in Curry's absence, combined to miss 20 of 23 shots.

    There's some reason for hope with this duo as this Curry-less stretch continues. This season, they have led the Warriors to a +2.6 net rating in their minutes without Curry, via Databallr. It's a very different story doing it without Curry for a few minutes while he rests on the bench, versus doing it for full games. But there's no time for learning curves here. This duo probably needs to score 40 points and create closer to 60 without Curry.

    The Warriors need to win in New Orleans on Monday. The Pelicans are kind of a mess right now, and Golden State getting to 9-5 would go a long way toward at least allowing Curry to return to a .500 team. After facing the Pelicans, the Warriors play the Mavericks and Grizzlies on a back-to-back, and then the Celtics in their first game back home. It's a hard stretch.

    Recent findings suggest that after that, it's the Kings on Nov. 25, which will be the two-week mark of Curry's timeline. The Warriors will cross their fingers that he can come back after that game, and in that case, even if they only beat the Pelicans and Kings over this stretch, they would still be 10-8 upon Curry's return.

    Even if Curry ends up missing an extra week or so, two of the Warriors' three games following the Kings matchup come against the 3-8 Clippers (who they have already beaten without Curry) and the 1-12 Jazz. They can still come out of this OK.

    The club had earlier released a statement on the incident that read:.

Another suggested that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate representing the state of Michigan.

    Championship hangover? Josh Hart 'not in a good headspace' as he, other Knicks struggle amid uneven start

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The New York Knicks slipped to 6-6 on Friday with a 106-104 loss to the Indiana Pacers, dropping into a tie for fifth in the Eastern Conference alongside the Miami Heat.
    • It has been revealed that while it hasn't been an outright disaster of a start, it has been an uneven performance by the defending champions that has left them frustrated and searching for answers.
    • After a scoreless performance against the Pacers, Josh Hart was brutally honest about not knowing what's wrong and how he's been struggling mentally to start this season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The New York Knicks slipped to 6-6 on Friday with a 106-104 loss to the Indiana Pacers, dropping into a tie for fifth in the Eastern Conference alongside the Miami Heat.

    It has been revealed that while it hasn't been an outright disaster of a start, it has been an uneven performance by the defending champions that has left them frustrated and searching for answers. The championship hangover in Newly introduced York seems to be real, and the once immaculate vibes at Madison Square Garden have been replaced by frustration as they try to get on track.

    After a scoreless performance against the Pacers, Josh Hart was brutally honest about not knowing what's wrong and how he's been struggling mentally to start this season.

    Sources indicate that "Wish I could tell you," Hart mentioned. "Don't know. Right now I'm not in a good headspace, and I got to figure out how to improve that and improve my play.".

    One of the strengths of the Knicks during their title run last year was their rotation of two-way wings between Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, but so far this season their three best wings -- OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Hart -- have been stuck in the mud offensively.

    Industry observers note that those three are all shooting below 40% from the field and below 33% from 3-point range this season, a massive departure from last season when they were all above 48% from the field and 37% from distance. The result of Latest York's wings struggling on offense -- aside from Landry Shamet, who has been a needed bright spot -- has been an even greater burden on Brunson and Towns.

    In a recent development, towns has been sensational, averaging 21.1 points and 13.7 rebounds per game on 54.2/40.0/77.0 shooting splits as he's moved back to a full-time role at center after the departure of Mitchell Robinson. Brunson has been his typically excellent self, averaging 26.6 points and 5.7 assists per game -- a slim uptick in points and a small decrease in assists from last year -- but his efficiency has dipped, shooting 43.6% from the field.

    According to recent reports, while his 3-point percentage has held firm at 37.5%, he's shooting just 55.8% from inside three feet. That would be the worst finishing rate of his career at the rim and seems to be a byproduct of teams collapsing in without the threat of spacing from the wings around Brunson.

    A less effective Brunson at the rim, the struggles of their wings and Towns playing more at the five have resulted in a Knicks offense that is 29th in the NBA in paint points at 35.5%. Mike Brown's offense is predicated on launching threes, but a year ago the Knicks got 41.4% of their points in the paint. A 6% drop-off there is a significant reduction, especially considering how poorly they're shooting from three as a team.

    The significant question raised by Hart's comments after Indiana's game is: how did the Knicks get here after winning the title?

    It's one thing to have a championship hangover, but it's another to have the vibes of a team sour so rapidly, considering their success was built in no small part on being a tight-knit group. It's hard not to point to the top of the organization and the way James Dolan seemed adamant about raining on the Knicks' championship celebration almost as soon as it began.

    Dolan didn't even let the champagne-soaked locker room dry out before he proclaimed his refusal to go into the second apron to keep the team together. He stayed true to his word, letting Robinson walk to the rival Boston Celtics. However, what was perhaps more impactful on this year's poor start is the way the Knicks handled extension talks with much of their roster.

    Towns made clear his desire to work out a deal to stay in Latest York and cut the Knicks a hometown discount, but New York was asking him to take an even bigger pay cut than he was willing. Ultimately, talks fell apart and the Knicks made the curious decision to publicly announce they were no longer going to discuss extensions with anyone on the roster a week before the season began.

    Hart is among the extension-eligible players, but unlike Towns, who can decline a player option and hit free agency, his option for next year is a $22.3 million team option. If the Knicks wanted, they could simply pick up Hart's option and extend discussions on a upcoming deal into next summer. One can't help but wonder whether the uncertainty about the future is part of whatis affecting Hart and putting him in a bad headspace.

    Some players thrive under the pressure of a contract year, while others just feel the anxiety of not having a stable future. Hart, whose impact often goes beyond the box score, might feel that more than others.

    Industry observers note that the Knicks had two paths they could've taken this summer after winning their first title in over 50 years. One was to do everything possible to lock up the core group as swiftly as possible and try to keep the good vibes rolling. The other was to play hardball and use the championship as an opportunity to squeeze players for a discount.

    Knicks fans weren't surprised to see Dolan choose option two, and now they have to wonder if that's at the root of an uneven start to their title defense.

    By IAN LADYMAN, FOOTBALL EDITOR.

    Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026.

    Next week Arsene Wenger will be in Qatar for the second staging of FIFA's 48-team Under-17 World Cup.

    Sources indicate that he described last year's inaugural event using one evocative word. 'Paradise,' he said. 'Basically, 25 per cent of the football world was here.'.

    At the end of last month – as the fall-out from FIFA president Gianni Infantino's foiled proposal to sell off parts of the men's senior World Cup rumbled on – Wenger was in Azerbaijan at the hosting of the very first Under-15 version.

    According to recent reports, an eight-a-side tournament with the emphasis on technique and quality, it was – in his role as FIFA's head of global development – another of his own ideas. According to those who know him, this is Wenger's happy place.

    'Arsene's vision is very simple,' one long-time ally tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It has always been that as many boys and girls as possible can participate in the game under as good a quality of coaching as is physically and financially possible.

    It has been revealed that 'That is it, basically. That is why he works for FIFA. He wants that direct influence on the game. He is 77 but fundamentally he is a coach at heart. In his own mind, he still has his whistle in his mouth and his stopwatch round his wrist.'.

    Industry observers note that arsene Wenger is FIFA's head of global development and many thought he'd challenge Gianni Infantino for the presidency of the organisation. Those hopes were misplaced.

    Wenger, the former Arsenal manager, is still a coach at heart according to those that know him well.

    Viewed in this context, it is perhaps not a surprise that Wenger is no longer expected to stand as a rival to Infantino at next March's presidential elections in Rabat. The deadline for nominations is on Wednesday.

    Industry observers note that wenger's fury at what he saw as Infantino's World Cup treachery was limitless. Some close to him feared he may quit in protest at an organisation he joined seven years ago. Others urged him to challenge Infantino's presidency, hoping it would serve to cleanse FIFA's reputation for sleaze.

    But even though as recently as last week Wenger's intentions remained unclear to many people within the organisation, the conflict raging inside his own head was crystal clear.

    'Arsene is an idealist and a romantic,' explains another source who has known him for 20 years. 'And the head of that organisation is not a place for someone like that. FIFA presidency is about glad-handing and politics and – let's face it – money.

    According to recent reports, 'Say what you like about Infantino, he's good at it. It's his natural habitat. He knows the rules. Arsene? He would lie awake at night wondering where all the money was going. He would be fretting about whether it was being spent in all the areas the different confederations told him it was.

    Industry observers note that 'On the one hand, Arsene would be a perfect figurehead for the global game. A purist. The total antithesis to Infantino's perceived chicanery. But in reality, how much could he change? Many of FIFA's reputational challenges are deeply embedded.'.

    The sub-plot to Wenger's emotional conflict regarding a direct challenge to Infantino is that inside FIFA it has had an all or nothing feel to it. The former Arsenal manager's contract in his current global development role expires at the end of this year and for all that the organisation would very much like him to renew, there remains the possibility that he may walk away.

    If Wenger doesn't – as we now expect – stand in opposition to Infantino, will he have the appetite to continue working underneath him?

    Wenger was furious with Infantino's foiled plan to sell off parts of the men's senior World Cup.

    Wenger with the Premier League trophy in 2004. 'Arsene would be a perfect figurehead for the global game. A purist,' says a source who knows him well.

    Wenger, for example, was a noticeable absentee when other FIFA leaders gathered to support Infantino at a management committee meeting in Morocco in August. The two men were not seen together again until they stood side by side at the Under-15 tournament last month.

    In a recent development, 'I think that (Wenger's future) is a very pertinent question,' adds another ally. 'It's on his mind and it's a big decision. To a much lesser degree, his age may well be a factor too. But he has the fire in his belly. He has energy. I know that.

    Industry observers note that 'He had a certain aim and certain targets when he started with FIFA. And he hasn't met them yet.'.

    Under Wenger's stewardship and guidance, FIFA have established 60 academies in previously under-resourced football backwaters such as India, Uzbekistan and New Caledonia.

    Industry observers note that 'We provide the structure, the finance and – by way of top coaches – the expertise,' explains a source from the governing body. 'For example, we have Spanish coaches leading the way in India. We basically have coaches coaching the coaches, if that makes sense.

    'Arsene believes every child in the world should have a pathway if they have the talent. India, for example, have never been to a senior men's World Cup. Arsene wants to change that.'.

    At last month's Under-15 World Cup, 500 players were involved who had emerged from Wenger's FIFA academies. The governing body's stated aim is to have established 75 by the end of next year.

    Recent findings suggest that 'In Arsene's mind, the number would actually be 100,' laughs his associate. 'And he knows he isn't there yet.'.

    Spain, watched by Infantino (left), raise the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan last month.

    The Under-15 World Cup was one of Wenger's ideas and is an eight-a-side tournament with the emphasis on technique and quality.

    According to recent reports, wenger is evangelical about it all. Some would – and do – say he remains a dreamer at heart. He also remains a small details person. For example, the reason he has established the Under-17 World Cup as an annual event is that he doesn't want a single talented footballer to fall through the cracks and miss out simply by being born a year too early or too late.

    The Frenchman is not, however, without his contradictions. Once asked privately how a father of a daughter could justify a FIFA decision to hold the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia – where the women's rights issue remains deeply contentious – Wenger suggested that he wished only to 'effect change from within'.

    It has been revealed that just as pertinent is the impact Wenger has undoubtedly had – for better or for worse – on football's global calendar. You don't have to have a particularly sharp memory to recall the many times Wenger railed against the dangers of too much travel and playing-time on his top players when he was in charge at Arsenal.

    Of all the top English clubs, Arsenal were the last to commit to arduous pre-season tours to places like America and the Far East and that was simply because Wenger was the manager. He always preferred a week in the Austrian mountains to a schlep round the world.

    Now – eight-and-a-half years on from his departure from the Emirates – Wenger has been firmly attached to FIFA's gravy train for some time, a driving force behind the expanded summer Club World Cup and a key advocate of a strategy to hold the World Cup every two years that ultimately didn't get off the ground.

    In a recent development, wenger is on record on the matter. 'The welfare of the players in the last 20 years has increased dramatically,' Wenger has mentioned. 'When you look at injury prevention, recovery work, nutrition and advances in medical technology. It is unrecognisable from what it used to be.

    'Also VAR has helped with the protection of players, as players know they cannot escape from making bad tackles that cause injury.'.

    Club coaches across Europe may raise eyebrows at that. So would many of those who opposed the expansion of this year's World Cup to 48 teams. But alternative theories are also in play.

    Asked how a father of a daughter could justify the decision to hold the 2034 World Cup in Saudi Arabia – where women's rights are deeply contentious – Wenger mentioned he only wished to 'effect change from within'.

    Many wanted Wenger to challenge Infantino's presidency, hoping it would serve to cleanse FIFA's reputation for sleaze.

    'Arsene was seen as poster boy for the two-year World Cup and, yes, he put his weight behind it,' explains our FIFA source. 'But in truth we were being asked that question by some member associations. It was FIFA's duty to look into it.

    Recent findings suggest that 'The mistake some people make is to look at everything from a European perspective. European football is blessed but not everybody is. Many countries just don't play as much competitive football and Arsene is strong on the global view.

    Industry observers note that 'He listened to the pushback but wants to give opportunities to clubs from smaller nations in things like the Club World Cup and a bigger World Cup. It's not just about England, France, Germany, Argentina and Brazil.

    In a recent development, 'When you are a club manager you are paid to be essentially selfish and when he looks back he recognises that. His horizons have been broadened. Some of the smaller nations don't have the calendar congestion that exists in England, for example. His principles remain the same but he has just seen another perspective.'.

    In a recent development, by his own self-effacing admission, Wenger has always led a rather monastic existence. Splitting his time between Zurich – where FIFA have their HQ – and his home in the north London enclave of Totteridge, he still endeavours to run 5km every morning. After that, it's football.

    'If there is football on TV from one of the leagues then I will watch it,' he told Mo Farah on a recent episode of the Olympic Champion's podcast. 'It's simply what I like to do.'.

    Recent findings suggest that it is not too simplistic to say that the sport remains Wenger's obsession. It is hard to imagine him without it at the core of his life. Equally, it is difficult to imagine a return to club football in any meaningful capacity.

    The wounds caused by what he felt was a rancorous departure from Arsenal have healed but that, nevertheless, remains a chapter closed.

    'Arsene was seen as poster boy for the two-year World Cup and, yes, he put his weight behind it,' explains our FIFA source.

    'Sir Alex Ferguson was capable of staying tight to Manchester United but for Arsene and Arsenal it was different'.

    Recent findings suggest that 'It would be disingenuous to say it wasn't all a bit distant and uncomfortable for a while,' states a source with knowledge of the situation. 'Arsene made a decision to step away from it completely. Sir Alex Ferguson was capable of staying tight to Manchester United but for Arsene and Arsenal it was different.

    Industry observers note that 'The ending was different for a start. So it was a bit like a divorce. You need some distance for a while before you can remember what you liked about each other back in the first place.

    According to recent reports, 'But that's where it is now. It's thawed. There is semi-regular contact. He's been back to a game, even if it was just the one.'.

    For Wenger, the pull of what he sees as unfinished business with FIFA may remain strong. Equally, beyond the rather waspish and phlegmatic public face has always run a river of steel.

    'You don't go toe to toe with Fergie all of those years and have all that personal c**p poured on you by Jose Mourinho and come out the other side in one piece if you haven't got some proper b***s,' indicates one of our sources.

    'Some of us were surprised how long it took him to come out and speak publicly about his opposition to Infantino's World Cup sell-off. It was discussed. But he got there in the end. The bottom line is that he has his principles and he already has his relevance. Infantino constantly has to fight for his. Arsene does not. If he isn't comfortable where he works, he will always find something else.'.

    It's a view thoroughly endorsed by just about everybody in Wenger's orbit. 'Whatever he does next – whether with FIFA or somewhere else – it will be in football,' adds an ally. 'The next chapter will be his decision. He is very focused. And there is already a legacy.'.

    Recent findings suggest that 'The bottom line is that Wenger has his principles and he already has his relevance. Infantino constantly has to fight for his'.

    Wenger and Infantino will in all likelihood be side by side in Doha next week as the second staging of FIFA's 48-team Under-17 World Cup gets into full swing.

    Sources indicate that wenger and Infantino will in all likelihood be side by side in Doha next week as the Under-17 jamboree gets into full swing. Teams from Tanzania, Mozambique and Vietnam will make their debut in the 104-match tournament. In Qatar, FIFA will present a thoroughly united front with Wenger's avowed principles at its core.

    'You can play with an orange or you can make a ball with paper,' Wenger told The Independent in a rare interview three years ago. 'That's why football is so popular. But today if you want to get to a good level of education in football, in some countries you don't get it.

    'I find that not right because, in many countries, there are some private initiatives, but the parents have to pay to get the children in there and play. For me, it doesn't matter if you're rich or poor. If you are good, you come in.

    'Our academies are free, just open to talent. You have to adapt and find a solution in every country.'.

    #73539. Breaking: NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Celtics win Jaylen Brown trade (for now), Trae Young looks done
